skill.summary: Configure and troubleshoot Uvicorn for Python ASGI applications.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: The 45 external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline option formatting; no backtick execution exists. Temporary socket usage, placeholder TLS paths, container binding, loopback documentation, and worker-option text are legitimate examples. Five examples bind to all interfaces without sufficient exposure warnings, and four also use development reload settings.

remediation.issue: Several examples bind to 0.0.0.0, and some enable reload without warning that the development server becomes network-accessible.
remediation.suggestion: Default development examples to 127.0.0.1. Require access controls and an explicit warning when external binding is necessary.

content.value_statement: Running ASGI applications requires correct server, reload, worker, logging, TLS, and container settings. This skill provides practical Uvicorn patterns for development and deployment.
actual_capabilities: Provides Uvicorn CLI patterns for hosts, ports, reload, workers, logging, TLS, and Unix sockets.
Shows ASGI, FastAPI, application factory, and programmatic server examples.
Explains environment variables and common command-line options.
Provides Dockerfile and Docker Compose deployment patterns.
Covers module paths, reload behavior, worker configuration, debugging, and health checks.
limitations: The skill provides guidance but does not install, run, or validate Uvicorn.
Examples assume that project modules, application objects, and dependencies already exist.
It does not cover reverse proxies, authentication, monitoring, orchestration, or complete production hardening.
Examples using 0.0.0.0 require network access controls to prevent unintended exposure.

use_cases.title: Start Local API Development
use_cases.description: Create a local Uvicorn setup with a safe host, chosen port, reload, and useful logs.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Production Deployment
use_cases.description: Select workers, TLS, process management, container settings, and health checks for an ASGI service.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Server Configuration
use_cases.description: Review module imports, reload directories, worker settings, ports, and logs when Uvicorn does not behave as expected.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Local FastAPI App
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Uvicorn command for [module]:[application]. Use localhost, port [port], and development reload. Explain each option.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an Application Factory
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to run [module]:[factory] as a Uvicorn application factory. Include environment settings for host, port, and logging.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Uvicorn setup for [application] with [workers] workers, access logs, TLS files, and a health endpoint. State exposure precautions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Container Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Uvicorn Dockerfile and Compose setup: [configuration]. Identify reload, worker, port, volume, and network issues. Propose corrected settings.

output_examples.input: Prepare a local FastAPI setup for main:app on port 8000.
output_examples.output: Recommended setup: run main:app on localhost port 8000 with reload enabled. Reload remains limited to development, and each setting is explained.

output_examples.input: Review a container configuration that publishes Uvicorn with reload and four workers.
output_examples.output: Review result: remove reload in production, verify worker support, keep container binding explicit, restrict host exposure, and add a health check.

best_practices: Use reload only for development and keep it separate from multi-worker production settings.
Bind to localhost unless remote access is required, then add firewall, proxy, or platform controls.
Keep TLS keys outside source control and restrict their filesystem permissions.
anti_patterns: Do not combine reload and multiple workers in one Uvicorn launch.
Do not expose a reload-enabled development server on every network interface.
Do not place private keys in source repositories or container images.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks can use this skill?
faq.answer: It applies to ASGI frameworks such as FastAPI, Starlette, Django Channels, and compatible custom applications.

faq.question: Does the skill install Uvicorn?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration guidance and examples. Install Uvicorn and project dependencies separately.

faq.question: Can I use reload in production?
faq.answer: No. Reload is intended for development and should not be combined with production worker settings.

faq.question: When should I bind to 0.0.0.0?
faq.answer: Use it only when external or container traffic must reach Uvicorn. Apply network controls and avoid development reload.

faq.question: Does the skill cover HTTPS?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows Uvicorn certificate and key options, but certificate creation and lifecycle management are outside its scope.

faq.question: Does the skill support Docker?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes basic Dockerfile and Docker Compose patterns for running Uvicorn.
